items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: Elvin Jones was really kind of more like Mel Lewis. They were really — so it was different.

ctx.x: Well you just said something that makes me think about, is there such a thing as playing on top of the beat or behind the beat?

Oh absolutely. Absolutely. This is what I also work with the bass players. Because we have the pulse. This is a quarter note: one-two-three-four one-two-three-four. But that’s not the pulse. The pulse is [hand gesture] and a bigger pulse is [hand gesture]. So there’s a lot of things that can be done within the pulse. And the beat is actually this wide, and the center of the beat is here. Some people play over here, some people play it here, some people play it here. That’s what it’s like, and this zone over here.…
Here it is, right here. You fit in.
